intro: Michigan's Graduated Driver Licensing starts at 14 years, 9 months. Our Michigan starter bank covers licensing and signs, pavement markings and signals from the official What Every Driver Must Know manual — more chapters are being verified.

commonMistakes.text: Crossing a solid white line to pass. In Michigan, that's illegal — solid white lines mark the road edge.
commonMistakes.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Solid white lines

commonMistakes.text: Carrying a car full of friends on a Level 2 license. You may have no more than one passenger under 21 unless an exception applies.
commonMistakes.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Your Driver's License — Graduated Driver Licensing: Level 2 Intermediate License

faq.q: How old must I be for a Michigan Level 1 Learner's License?
How many supervised hours does Michigan require?
faq.a: A minimum of 50 hours, including 10 hours at night, and you must hold your Level 1 license for at least six months.

questions.question: What is the minimum age for a Michigan Level 1 Learner's License?
questions.explanation: You must be at least 14 years, 9 months old for a Level 1 Learner's License.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Your Driver's License — Graduated Driver Licensing: Level 1 Learner's License

questions.question: Who may supervise a Michigan Level 1 driver?
options: A licensed parent, guardian or designated licensed adult 21 or older seated in the front seat
Any adult in the back seat
A sibling with a Level 2 license
questions.correctAnswer: A licensed parent, guardian or designated licensed adult 21 or older seated in the front seat
questions.explanation: Level 1 drivers must be accompanied by a licensed parent, guardian or designated licensed adult age 21 or older seated in the front seat.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Your Driver's License — Graduated Driver Licensing: Level 1 Learner's License

questions.question: How many hours of supervised driving must a Michigan Level 1 driver complete?
options: At least 50 hours, including 10 at night
questions.correctAnswer: At least 50 hours, including 10 at night
questions.explanation: Level 1 drivers must complete a minimum of 50 hours of supervised driving, including 10 hours at night.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Your Driver's License — Graduated Driver Licensing: Level 1 Learner's License

questions.question: How long must you hold a Michigan Level 1 Learner's License before moving on?
questions.explanation: You must have held your Level 1 Learner's License for at least six months.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Your Driver's License — Graduated Driver Licensing: Level 1 Learner's License

questions.question: With a Michigan Level 2 Intermediate License, when may you generally NOT drive (without an exception)?
questions.explanation: Level 2 drivers may not drive between 10 p.m. and 5 a.m. unless accompanied by an authorized adult, driving for employment or going to/from an authorized activity.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Your Driver's License — Graduated Driver Licensing: Level 2 Intermediate License

questions.question: With a Michigan Level 2 Intermediate License, how many passengers under 21 may you carry (without an exception)?
questions.explanation: You may not have more than one passenger under 21 unless an authorized adult is present, passengers are immediate family, or you are driving for employment or an authorized activity.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 1: Your Driver's License — Graduated Driver Licensing: Level 2 Intermediate License

questions.question: In Michigan, which sign shape means STOP?
questions.explanation: Michigan's driver manual shows that an octagon means STOP.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Traffic signs

questions.question: In Michigan, a triangle-shaped sign means:
questions.explanation: A triangle-shaped sign means YIELD.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Traffic signs

questions.question: In Michigan, a diamond-shaped sign indicates:
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs indicate a WARNING.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Traffic signs

questions.question: In Michigan, a pentagon-shaped sign means:
questions.explanation: A pentagon-shaped sign means SCHOOL.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Traffic signs

questions.question: According to Michigan's manual, what does a sign's shape tell you?
options: It gives a clue to the sign's meaning and purpose
questions.correctAnswer: It gives a clue to the sign's meaning and purpose
questions.explanation: A traffic sign's shape gives you a clue as to its meaning and purpose.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Traffic signs

questions.question: In Michigan, a red traffic sign color means:
questions.explanation: Red means stop, prohibited or forbidden.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Traffic sign colors

questions.question: In Michigan, orange traffic signs mean:
questions.explanation: Orange means caution for construction or maintenance.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Traffic sign colors

questions.question: In Michigan, fluorescent yellow-green signs warn about:
questions.explanation: Fluorescent yellow-green means school, pedestrian or bicycle caution.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Traffic sign colors

questions.question: In Michigan, green traffic signs provide:
questions.explanation: Green signs provide directions and guidance.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Traffic sign colors

questions.question: In Michigan, broken white lines:
options: Separate traffic moving in opposite directions
Separate traffic lanes moving in the same direction
questions.correctAnswer: Separate traffic lanes moving in the same direction
questions.explanation: Broken white lines separate traffic lanes moving in the same direction.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Broken white lines

questions.question: In Michigan, is it legal to cross a solid white line when passing?
questions.explanation: Solid white lines mark the right edge of the road, and it is illegal to cross solid white lines when passing.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Solid white lines

questions.question: In Michigan, a single broken yellow line usually marks:
options: The right edge of the road
The center of a two-way road where you may pass if it is safe
questions.correctAnswer: The center of a two-way road where you may pass if it is safe
questions.explanation: A single broken yellow line usually marks the center line of a two-way roadway where a vehicle may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Broken yellow lines

questions.question: A double solid yellow line down the middle of a Michigan two-lane road means:
options: Passing is not allowed for vehicles traveling in either direction
questions.correctAnswer: Passing is not allowed for vehicles traveling in either direction
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means passing is not allowed for vehicles traveling in either direction.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Solid yellow lines

questions.question: Where is the red light located on a Michigan traffic signal?
questions.explanation: The red light is at the top of a traffic signal in Michigan.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Traffic signals

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean in Michigan?
options: Come to a full stop, then proceed when the road is clear
The signal is about to turn green
questions.correctAnswer: Come to a full stop, then proceed when the road is clear
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means come to a full stop and proceed when the road is clear.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Traffic signals

questions.question: On a Michigan 5-section signal head, what does a lit green arrow give turning drivers?
options: A protected turn — conflicting traffic is stopped
questions.correctAnswer: A protected turn — conflicting traffic is stopped
questions.explanation: When the green arrow is lit, turning drivers have a protected turn, meaning all oncoming or conflicting traffic is stopped.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — The 5-section-head signal

questions.question: In Michigan, a green light means:
options: Proceed with caution after checking for pedestrians and vehicles
Stop if a pedestrian is nearby
questions.correctAnswer: Proceed with caution after checking for pedestrians and vehicles
questions.explanation: A green light means proceed with caution after checking for pedestrians and vehicles.
questions.sourceTitle: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan Department of State)
questions.sourceSection: Chapter 5: Signs, Pavement Markings and Signals — Traffic signals
